Stated Claim / Post Context:
Hillary Clinton admits it was 'a mistake' to keep pneumonia diagnosis hidden and keep campaigning before infamous 2016 fainting scare

Clinton, 78, made the concession on the inaugural episode of her new podcast with progressive CNN contributor Kara Swisher, while discussing the midterm elections.

Actual Article Body:
By ALEX HAMMER, US MEDIA CORRESPONDENT

Updated:  07:46 AEDT, 16 October 2026

Hillary Clinton admitted Wednesday that she made a 'mistake' by continuing to campaign with a case of pneumonia back in 2016.

Clinton, 78, made the concession on the inaugural episode of her new podcast with progressive CNN contributor Kara Swisher, while discussing the midterm elections.

Clinton was diagnosed with pneumonia on September 9, 2016, and advised to rest, she's previously said.

Instead, she chose to attend a 9/11 commemoration ceremony in Manhattan two days later. She infamously suffered a fainting spell while being rushed into a car before the ceremony was over.

Speaking to CNN about it the following day, she said she did not disclose the diagnosis because 'I just didn't think it was going to be that big a deal.'

Clinton's communications director at the time, Jennifer Palmieri, framed the silence as the result of poor management.

More than ten years later, Clinton compared rumors currently plaguing Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico spurred by a nine-day absence from the campaign trail because of a case of the flu to discourse surrounding her condition.

'They, you know, painted me like I was on death's door,' she recalled.

Hillary Clinton admitted that she made a 'mistake' by continuing to campaign with a case of pneumonia back in 2016 on Wednesday.

Donald Trump, then the GOP’s presidential nominee, used footage of her knees buckling to bolster his claims that Clinton lacked the physical health and stamina for the presidency.

She went on to lose the election two months later, in what many viewed as a monumental upset.

'I, uh, kept going, which was a mistake,' Clinton told Swisher.

'They did have the video of me struggling to get to the car to be able to, you know, take some breaths and recover myself.

'From my perspective, it worked because it was just papering social media, papering traditional media: "I was dying. I was lying about my health."'

'This is from a guy who has never given us an honest medical report ever. Ever,' Clinton continued.

Trump has had four publicly disclosed medical exams since the president's second term began last year.

The Daily Mail has approached Clinton's team for comment.

Clinton, 78, made the concession on the inaugural episode of her new podcast with progressive CNN contributor Kara Swisher

Clinton and Swisher's new show, 'High Stakes,' is focused around the midterms, but could continue once they conclude if it attracts a large enough audience, the former secretary of state told The New York Times while plugging the podcast on Tuesday.

'I don’t think the stakes for our country and the world have ever been higher than they are in November,' Clinton said in a statement.

'People are hungry for real conversation about what’s happening in our democracy and what it will mean for their families, and I can’t think of a better partner for that than Kara.'

The podcast was announced on Tuesday.
